title: Your $7 Coffee Could Become $45,500
segments: Your seven-dollar coffee isn't ruining your finances. Relax. But buying it on autopilot? That could be a different story.
One coffee, five weekdays a week, fifty weeks a year. That's thirty-five dollars a week... and seventeen hundred and fifty dollars a year. Your coffee cup has a subscription plan.
Now imagine putting that same thirty-five dollars a week to work instead. Every week, for fifty weeks a year, over fifteen years.

At a hypothetical seven percent annual return, compounded weekly, that could grow to roughly forty-five thousand five hundred dollars. You put in twenty-six thousand two hundred and fifty. The rest is hypothetical investment growth.
Big disclaimer: seven percent is not guaranteed. Markets can fall. Fees, taxes, and inflation can reduce what you actually get. This is an illustration, not a promise.
And no, you don't have to break up with coffee. Just stop paying for habits you don't even enjoy. Your wallet deserves better taste too.
Choose one small expense you barely notice. Redirect it toward a goal you actually care about. Follow The Money Stickman for money lessons without the boring lecture.
